ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p336/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p336/r9.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p336/r9.claim: Khabbāb says they saw the wealth of Banū Qurayẓa, al-Naḍīr, and Qaynuqāʿ and wished for it before the verse about unrestricted provision came down.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p336/r9.anchor: وقال خباب بن الأرت: نظرنا إلى أموال بني قريظة والنضير وبني قينقاع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p336/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p336/r10.speaker: عمرو بن حريث
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p336/r10.claim: ʿAmr b. Ḥurayth says people of the Suffa asked the Prophet for wealth and abundance, prompting the verse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p336/r10.anchor: وقال عمرو بن حريث: طلب قوم من أهل الصفة من الرسول عليه السلام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p336/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p336/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p336/r11.claim: If provision followed human preferences, it would lead to oppression; God knows each person's best condition, since some need poverty and others prosperity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p336/r11.anchor: أعلم أن الرزق لو جاء على اقتراح البشر، لكان سبب بغيهم وإفسادهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p337/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p337/r1.speaker: أنس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p337/r1.claim: Anas reports a prayer asking not to be impoverished because the speaker is among those whom only wealth can set right.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p337/r1.anchor: حديث رواه أنس وقال: «اللهم إني من عبادك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p337/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p337/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p337/r2.claim: بغوا may mean becoming arrogant through affluence, as in the example of Qārūn; a prophetic report fears the allure of worldly bloom.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p337/r2.anchor: ولبغوا، إما من البذخ والكبر، أي لتكبروا في الأرض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p337/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p337/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p337/r3.claim: A poet illustrates how prosperity can prompt people to seek conflict and discord between tribes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p337/r3.anchor: وقال الشاعر: وقد جعلوا الوسمي ينبت بيننا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p337/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p337/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p337/r4.claim: ينزل بقدر means God apportions what is most suitable for people.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p337/r4.anchor: ولكن ينزل بقدر ما يشاء، يقال: قدر بالسكون وبالفتح

STUDYQURAN:42:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:42:intro/r3.speaker: Āl
STUDYQURAN:42:intro/r3.claim: Some add verse 27 as Madinan, reading it as a reference to the poorest members of the Madinan community, the People of the Veranda.
STUDYQURAN:42:intro/r3.anchor: understood as a reference to the poorest members of the nascent Muslim community in Madinah, known as the People of the Veranda (Āl;

STUDYQURAN:42:intro/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:42:intro/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:42:intro/r11.claim: God is Provider and Sustainer, owns the keys of heaven and earth, and distributes provision by wisdom; this applies to wealth, offspring, and revelation.
STUDYQURAN:42:intro/r11.anchor: the Provider and Sustainer unto Whom belong the keys of the heavens and the earth (v. 12) and Who provides as He wills in accord with His Wisdom

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p143/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p143/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p143/r4.claim: The affluent are mistaken if they take their riches as proof that they are on the right path or as grounds for arrogance toward the Prophet and poorer believers.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p143/r4.anchor: if their worldly affluence and riches have led them to believe that they are on the right path

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p143/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p143/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p143/r5.claim: God apportions wealth to believers and disbelievers according to wisdom and circumstances to test whether they remain patient and grateful; unrestricted riches could lead to rebellion.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p143/r5.anchor: per His wisdom and expedience, and in this manner tries them both.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p143/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p143/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p143/r6.claim: Recipients should thank God rather than credit their own ability or forebears, since He can grant wealth and take it away.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p143/r6.anchor: he should remain grateful to God Who has the authority to give and also to take away after giving.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p143/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p143/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p143/r7.claim: He says the subject of wealth distribution is treated in more detail in the following sūrah, al-Zukhruf, which parallels this one.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p143/r7.anchor: This subject is discussed in more detail in the succeeding sūrah: Sūrah al-Zukhruf

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p144/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p144/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p144/r1.claim: The counterpart sūrah elaborates that God assigns different livelihoods and ranks so people serve one another, while worldly riches are temporary and success belongs to the virtuous.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p144/r1.anchor: We have allocated among them their livelihood in this world and have raised some in status above others

MUQATIL:42:27-32/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:42:27-32/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:42:27-32/r1.claim: If God expanded provision for all His servants at once, they would rebel; instead He apportions it as He wills, knowing and seeing them. “In the earth” is fronted in the sentence.
MUQATIL:42:27-32/r1.anchor: يعنى ولو وسع الله الرزق، { لعباده } ، فى ساعة واحدة، { لبغوا } ، يعنى لعصوا، { في الأرض } ، فيها تقديم

RAZI-FULL:v27p146#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p146#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p146#2/r1.claim: The previous verse says God answers believers' prayers, raising the question why a believer in hardship may pray without seeing an apparent answer; this verse explains the wisdom in limiting provision.
RAZI-FULL:v27p146#2/r1.anchor: لما قال في الآية الأولى : إنه يجيب دعاء المؤمنين ورد عليه سؤال وهو أن المؤمن قد يكون

RAZI-FULL:v27p146#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p146#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p146#2/r2.claim: God limits expansion because it would lead people to sins, a harmful outcome; this explains why believers may not receive everything they request.
RAZI-FULL:v27p146#2/r2.anchor: أي ولأقدموا على المعاصي ، ولما كان ذلك محذورا وجب أن يعطيهم ما طلبوه

RAZI-FULL:v27p146#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p146#2/r3.speaker: الجبائي
RAZI-FULL:v27p146#2/r3.claim: Al-Jubbai argues that if God does not will transgression, He cannot will expanded provision that would produce it; he says this challenges the determinists.
RAZI-FULL:v27p146#2/r3.anchor: قال الجبائي : هذه الآية تدل على بطلان قول المجبرة من وجهين

RAZI-FULL:v27p146#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p146#2/r4.speaker: الجبائي
RAZI-FULL:v27p146#2/r4.claim: Al-Jubbai's second argument is that if God declines an increase because it leads to evil, a fortiori He does not will the evil itself.
RAZI-FULL:v27p146#2/r4.anchor: أنه تعالى بين أنه إنما لم يرد بسط الرزق لأنه يفضي إلى المفسدة

RAZI-FULL:v27p146#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p146#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p146#2/r5.claim: Al-Razi responds that transgressive inclination arises after being absent and must have a cause; it cannot originate in the servant without an earlier inclination, producing an infinite regress.
RAZI-FULL:v27p146#2/r5.anchor: الميل الشديد إلى البغي والقسوة والقهر صفة حدثت بعد أن لم تكن فلا بد لها من فاعل

RAZI-FULL:v27p146#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p146#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p146#2/r6.claim: Al-Razi concludes God creates the inclination, since harshness and oppression are defects and a rational person would not produce causes of his own deficiency.
RAZI-FULL:v27p146#2/r6.anchor: ولما بطل هذا ثبت أن محدث هذا الميل والرغبة هو الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v27p146#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p146#2/r7.speaker: الجبائي
RAZI-FULL:v27p146#2/r7.claim: Al-Jubbai asks whether God gave wealth to some who then transgressed; he answers they were known to transgress whether or not they received it.
RAZI-FULL:v27p146#2/r7.anchor: ثم أورد الجبائي في ( تفسيره ) على نفسه سؤالا قال : فإن قيل أليس قد بسط الله الرزق لبعض عباده

RAZI-FULL:v27p146#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p146#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p146#2/r8.claim: Al-Razi rejects that reply: the Quran says humans transgress when they see themselves wealthy, and reason says an evil-leaning person does more harm when wealth supplies the means.
RAZI-FULL:v27p146#2/r8.anchor: حكم مطلقا بأن حصول الغنى سبب لحصول الطغيان

RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r1.claim: One explanation is that equal provision would eliminate service between people, ruining the world's order and disabling its benefits.
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r1.anchor: الأول : أن الله تعالى لو سوى في الرزق بين الكل لامتنع كون البعض خادما للبعض

RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r2.claim: A second explanation limits the verse to Arabs: when rain and abundant pasture enlarged their means, they resorted to raiding and pillaging.
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r2.anchor: الثاني : أن هذه الآية مختصة بالعرب فإنه كلما اتسع رزقهم ووجدوا من المطر ما يرويهم

RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r3.claim: A third explanation says wealth and power revive humans' innate pride, while distress humbles them and returns them to obedience.
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r3.anchor: الثالث : أن الإنسان متكبر بالطبع فإذا وجد الغنى والقدرة عاد إلى مقتضى خلقته الأصلية

RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r4.speaker: خباب بن الأرث
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r4.claim: Khabbab ibn al-Aratt says the verse was revealed about them when they saw the wealth of Banu Qurayza, Banu al-Nadir, and Banu Qaynuqa and coveted it.
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r4.anchor: قال خباب بن الأرث فينا نزلت هذه الآية وذلك أنا نظرنا إلى أموال بني قريظة والنضير

RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r5.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r5.claim: Another report says the People of the Bench wished for plentiful provision and wealth when the verse was revealed about them.
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r5.anchor: وقيل نزلت في أهل الصفة تمنوا سعة الرزق والغنى

RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r6.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r6.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read ينزل lightly; the other reciters read it with doubling.
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r6.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو { ينزل } خفيفة والباقون بالتشديد

RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r7.claim: بقدر means by measure or apportionment; the noun is used in the forms qadr and qadar.
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r7.anchor: ثم نقول { بقدر } بتقدير يقال قدره قدرا وقدرا

RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r8.claim: God knows people's conditions, temperaments, and outcomes, so He apportions their livelihoods in line with their interests.
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r8.anchor: يعني أنه عالم بأحوال الناس وبطباعهم وبعواقب أمورهم فيقدر أرزاقهم على وفق مصالحهم

STUDYQURAN:42:27/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:42:27/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:42:27/r1.claim: In context with 42:26, the verse directs attention toward increase in the Hereafter rather than worldly increase and clarifies the goodness promised in 42:23.
STUDYQURAN:42:27/r1.anchor: this verse emphasizes that one’s focus should be upon increase in the Hereafter rather than in this world

STUDYQURAN:42:27/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:42:27/r2.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:42:27/r2.claim: The verse is reported to have been revealed about poor early believers who longed for worldly wealth and ease.
STUDYQURAN:42:27/r2.anchor: some of the poor and destitute among the early believers who desired the wealth and ease of this world (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:42:27/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:42:27/r3.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:42:27/r3.claim: Some identify the occasion specifically with the homeless emigrants called the People of the Veranda.
STUDYQURAN:42:27/r3.anchor: Some say that it pertained specifically to the homeless emigrants known as the“People of the Veranda” (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:42:27/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:42:27/r4.speaker: Bg, Q
STUDYQURAN:42:27/r4.claim: The People of the Veranda may have coveted the wealth of other tribes in Madinah.
STUDYQURAN:42:27/r4.anchor: who may have looked with desire upon the wealth of other tribes in Madinah (Bg, Q)

STUDYQURAN:42:27/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:42:27/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:42:27/r5.claim: Greater provision could lead people to transgress God’s limits through tyranny and disobedience.
STUDYQURAN:42:27/r5.anchor: they would transgress the limits set by God (Ṭ) by being tyrannical and acting disobediently toward Him (Q)

STUDYQURAN:42:27/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:42:27/r6.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:42:27/r6.claim: The illustration of successive houses, mounts, and outfits means that people given much wealth would only seek more.
STUDYQURAN:42:27/r6.anchor: one abode, then another, one mount and then another, one outfit and then another (Q)

STUDYQURAN:42:27/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:42:27/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:42:27/r7.claim: A famous hadith says that a person with a valley of gold would wish for a second valley.
STUDYQURAN:42:27/r7.anchor: a famous ḥadīth, “If the son of Adam had a valley of gold, he would wish that he had two valleys”

STUDYQURAN:42:27/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:42:27/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:42:27/r8.claim: God apportions provision according to what He knows will benefit and suffice His servants.
STUDYQURAN:42:27/r8.anchor: God gives provision according to what He knows to be in the best interest of His servants (IK) and what suffices them (Q)

STUDYQURAN:42:27/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:42:27/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:42:27/r9.claim: A reduction in provision is not humiliation, and an increase is not necessarily a sign of Divine Favor.
STUDYQURAN:42:27/r9.anchor: reduction of provision is not abasement and increase in provision is not necessarily a sign of Divine Favor (Q)

STUDYQURAN:42:27/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:42:27/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:42:27/r10.claim: A hadith qudsī says that some believers are made righteous only through wealth while others are made righteous only through poverty; the opposite condition would corrupt each group.
STUDYQURAN:42:27/r10.anchor: as in aḥadīth qudsī, “Among My believing servants are those for whom nothing but wealth will make them righteous

TAB-FULL:v20p509/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p509/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p509/r1.claim: If God expanded provision, people would exceed His limits and commit what He forbade; instead He apportions what He wills to suffice them.
TAB-FULL:v20p509/r1.anchor: لبغوا، فتجاوزوا الحد الذي حده الله لهم إلى غير الذي حده لهم في بلاده بركوبهم في الأرض ما حظره عليهم

TAB-FULL:v20p509/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p509/r2.speaker: عمرو بن حريث
TAB-FULL:v20p509/r2.claim: Abu Hani reports Amr ibn Hurayth and others saying the verse concerned the impoverished Companions of the Bench, who wished for greater wealth.
TAB-FULL:v20p509/r2.anchor: سمعت عمرو بن حريث، وغيره، يقولون: " إنما أنزلت هذه الآية في أصحاب الصفة

TAB-FULL:v20p509/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p509/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v20p509/r3.claim: Qatadah cites the saying that the best provision is what neither makes a person tyrannical nor distracts them.
TAB-FULL:v20p509/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، {ولو بسط الله الرزق لعباده لبغوا في الأرض} [الشورى: 27] الآية قال: " كان يقال: خير الرزق ما لا يطغيك ولا يلهيك "

TAB-FULL:v20p509/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p509/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v20p509/r4.claim: Qatadah transmits a Prophetic warning about worldly abundance; wealth used for God’s prescribed path is good, while spending it on desires and neglecting God’s rights is evil.
TAB-FULL:v20p509/r4.anchor: وذكر لنا أن نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «أخوف ما أخاف على أمتي زهرة الدنيا وكثرتها»

BURSEVI:v8p244/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p244/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p244/r1.claim: بسط الرزق means making provision abundant and expansive.
BURSEVI:v8p244/r1.anchor: {ولو بسط الله الرزق لعباده} ، لو وسعه عليهم

BURSEVI:v8p244/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p244/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p244/r2.claim: بغى may mean transgressing and disobeying, oppressing one another, or pride as a metonym for corruption; wealth commonly brings insolence and arrogance.
BURSEVI:v8p244/r2.anchor: لطغوا في الأرض وعصوا ، فمن العصمة أن لا تجد

BURSEVI:v8p244/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p244/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v8p244/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains their transgression as seeking ever higher status, a better mount, and finer clothing.
BURSEVI:v8p244/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : بغيهم في الأرض طلبهم

BURSEVI:v8p244/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p244/r4.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v8p244/r4.claim: Some say that if God provided without requiring work, people would have leisure for corruption; keeping them occupied with earning prevents that, as the verse of poetry says youth, leisure, and wealth ruin a person.
BURSEVI:v8p244/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم : لو أن الله تعالى رزق العباد من غير كسب

BURSEVI:v8p244/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p244/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p244/r5.claim: Abundant provision usually increases transgression, though a poor person can also be arrogant and unjust; poverty more often humbles, while wealth more often provokes rebellion, so universal abundance would make corruption prevail.
BURSEVI:v8p244/r5.anchor: لأن الفقر مؤد إلى الانكسار والتواضع غالبا

BURSEVI:v8p244/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p244/r6.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v8p244/r6.claim: Al-Kāshifī says the rule is general, not universal: ʿUthmān was among the wealthiest people without visible transgression; worldly wealth is like rain that yields different growth from different soils.

BURSEVI:v8p244/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p244/r7.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v8p244/r7.claim: Al-Kāshifī explains that most people lean toward desire and animal or predatory traits; wealth is a powerful cause, so greatly expanding provision would make most people transgress, as Pharaoh, Hāmān, and Qārūn illustrate.
BURSEVI:v8p244/r7.anchor: وكفى بحال فرعون وهامان وقارون ونحوهم عبرة

BURSEVI:v8p244/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p244/r8.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v8p244/r8.claim: A Prophetic saying states that the thing most feared for the community is worldly abundance and its flowering; no grading is given.
BURSEVI:v8p244/r8.anchor: قال عليه السلام : "إن أخوف ما أخاف على أمتي

BURSEVI:v8p244/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p244/r9.speaker: الصائب
BURSEVI:v8p244/r9.claim: Al-Ṣāʾib’s poem warns against indulging the soul with worldly comforts: bread and water and satiation make the laborer idle.
BURSEVI:v8p244/r9.anchor:
قال الصائب :
نفس رابد خوبناز ونعمت دنيا مكن

BURSEVI:v8p244#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p244#2/r1.speaker: كشف الأسرار
BURSEVI:v8p244#2/r1.claim: Kashf al-asrar glosses بقدر as apportioning the provision by measure.

BURSEVI:v8p244#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p244#2/r2.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v8p244#2/r2.claim: Al-Kashifi interprets the apportionment as an eternal decree.

BURSEVI:v8p244#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p244#2/r3.speaker: القاموس
BURSEVI:v8p244#2/r3.claim: Al-Qamus defines measuring provision as dividing it, and qadr as measuring one thing against another.
BURSEVI:v8p244#2/r3.anchor: وفي "القاموس" : قدر الرزق : قسمه ، والقدر قياس الشيء بالشيء.

BURSEVI:v8p244#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p244#2/r4.speaker: بحر العلوم
BURSEVI:v8p244#2/r4.claim: Bahr al-Ulum records قدره with two verbal-noun forms, qadr and qadar.
BURSEVI:v8p244#2/r4.anchor: وفي "بحر العلوم" : يقال : قدره قدرا وقدرا.

BURSEVI:v8p244#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p244#2/r5.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v8p244#2/r5.claim: The Prophet instructs people to estimate the lunar month when the crescent is obscured, completing thirty days.
BURSEVI:v8p244#2/r5.anchor: وقوله عليه السلام : "فإن غم عليكم ، فاقدروا"

BURSEVI:v8p244#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p244#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p244#2/r6.claim: Bursevi reads the dāl of فاقدروا with kasra and rejects its pronunciation with damma as erroneous.

BURSEVI:v8p244#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p244#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p244#2/r7.claim: ما يشاء specifies what He wills to send and serves as the direct object of ينزل.
BURSEVI:v8p244#2/r7.anchor: أن ينزله مما تقتضيه مشيئته ، وهو مفعول ينزل.

BURSEVI:v8p244#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p244#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p244#2/r8.claim: God knows servants’ hidden and manifest states and apportions poverty, wealth, withholding, giving, constriction, or ease as wisdom fits each time; universal wealth would invite rebellion, universal poverty ruin.
BURSEVI:v8p244#2/r8.anchor: محيط بخفايا أمورهم وجلاياها ، فيقدر لكل واحد منهم في كل وقت

BURSEVI:v8p244#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p244#2/r9.speaker: أنس بن مالك
BURSEVI:v8p244#2/r9.claim: Anas says God wars on harm to friends; duties and extra worship bring love, senses, and answers; taking a believer’s soul grieves Him but must happen; He withholds worship and assigns poverty, wealth, health, or illness to protect faith.
BURSEVI:v8p244#2/r9.anchor: روى أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه ، عن النبي عليه السلام ، عن جبرائيل ، عن الله تعالى أنه قال : "من أهان لي وليا بارزني بالمحاربة

TABATABAI:42:27/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:27/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:27/r1.claim: The passage continues the discussion of provision in 42:19 and follows the statement in 42:12 that God expands and restricts provision.
TABATABAI:42:27/r1.anchor: متصل بحديث الرزق المذكور في قوله

TABATABAI:42:27/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:27/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:27/r2.claim: Religious guidance is also a provision God gives believers, so discussion of provision folds back into the sūra’s subject of revelation.
TABATABAI:42:27/r2.anchor: من الرزق نعمة الدين التي آتاها الله سبحانه عباده المؤمنين

TABATABAI:42:27/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:27/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:27/r3.claim: The ensuing signs of unity tied to provision include creating the heavens and Earth, spreading creatures, ships at sea, and granting children or barrenness as He wills.
TABATABAI:42:27/r3.anchor: ثم يذكر بعض آيات التوحيد المتعلقة بالرزق كخلق السماوات والأرض وبث الدواب فيهما والسفائن الجواري في البحر

TABATABAI:42:27/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:27/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:27/r4.claim: The discourse contrasts fleeting worldly provision with the better, lasting provision of the afterlife, then turns to believers’ qualities and the fate of wrongdoers.
TABATABAI:42:27/r4.anchor: من الرزق ما آتاهموه في الدنيا وهو متاعها الفاني بفنائها ومنه ما يخص المؤمنين في الآخرة وهو خير وأبقى

TABATABAI:42:27/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:27/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:27/r5.claim: The following verses also contain summaries of rulings, warnings, admonition, calls to truth, and many points of doctrine.
TABATABAI:42:27/r5.anchor: من إجمال بعض الأحكام والإنذار والتخويف والدعوة إلى الحق وحقائق المعارف شيء كثير

TABATABAI:42:27/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:27/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:27/r6.claim: Al-qadr here is the opposite of expansion: restriction, as in the earlier statement that God expands and restricts provision.

TABATABAI:42:27/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:27/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:27/r7.claim: Qadr, with either vowel on the dāl, means an amount or measure, or setting something to a determined measure; he cites 77:23 for the latter usage.
TABATABAI:42:27/r7.anchor: والقدر بفتح الدال وسكونها كمية الشيء وهندسته

TABATABAI:42:27/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:27/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:27/r9.claim: The explicit phrase “His servants” in place of a pronoun points to why God knows them: they are His created servants, sustained by Him and not hidden from Him.
TABATABAI:42:27/r9.anchor: وضع الظاهر موضع الضمير، والنكتة فيه الإشارة

TABATABAI:42:27/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:27/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:27/r10.claim: The earlier wording “for His servants” likewise hints at the grant of provision: a servant’s provision comes from his master.
TABATABAI:42:27/r10.anchor: لا يخلو من إشارة إلى بيان إيتاء الرزق

TABATABAI:42:27/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:27/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:27/r11.claim: If God made everyone’s provision abundant enough to satisfy them, they would tyrannize because wealth tends to produce pride, ingratitude, arrogance, and transgression; he links this to 96:6–7.
TABATABAI:42:27/r11.anchor: من طبع سعة المال الأشر والبطر والاستكبار والطغيان

TABATABAI:42:27#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:27#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:27#2/r1.claim: God apportions what each servant deserves and what will improve that servant’s condition, whether wealth or poverty, because He knows them fully.
TABATABAI:42:27#2/r1.anchor: فيعلم ما يستحقه كل عبد وما يصلحه من غنى أو فقر فيؤتيه ذلك

TABATABAI:42:27#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:27#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:27#2/r2.claim: The baseline divine practice is to measure provision with regard to what will set people’s condition right; their welfare affects the amount allotted.
TABATABAI:42:27#2/r2.anchor: بيان للسنة الإلهية في إيتاء الرزق بالنظر إلى صلاح حال الناس أي إن لصلاح حالهم أثرا في تقدير أرزاقهم

TABATABAI:42:27#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:27#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:27#2/r3.claim: The prosperity of some wealthy wrongdoers does not refute this rule, since a separate rule makes wealth and children a trial.

TABATABAI:42:27#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:27#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:27#2/r4.claim: Another rule is entrapment and gradual reprieve, by which God increases the resources of some wrongdoers without their awareness.
TABATABAI:42:27#2/r4.anchor: وسنة أخرى هي سنة المكر والاستدراج

TABATABAI:42:27#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:27#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:27#2/r5.claim: The reforming measure is the initial rule; God may test people, or change His treatment after they change themselves and turn blessing into ingratitude.
TABATABAI:42:27#2/r5.anchor: فسنة الإصلاح بتقدير الرزق سنة ابتدائيه يصلح بها حال الإنسان إلا أن يمتحنه الله

TABATABAI:42:27#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:27#2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:27#2/r6.claim: Material blessings, children, true knowledge, and revealed laws are all apportioned forms of provision, including the process of receiving and practicing revelation.
TABATABAI:42:27#2/r6.anchor: كذلك المعارف الحقة والشرائع السماوية المنتهية إلى الوحي من حيث إنزالها ومن حيث الابتلاء بها والتلبس بالعمل بها من الرزق المقسوم

TABATABAI:42:27#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:27#2/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:27#2/r7.claim: Revealing all comprehensive religious knowledge and law at once would overwhelm people; God instead sent it gradually, preparing acceptance step by step.
TABATABAI:42:27#2/r7.anchor: لكن الله سبحانه أنزلها على رسوله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم تدريجا وعلى مكث وهيأ بذلك الناس بقبول بعضها لقبول بعض

TABATABAI:42:27#2/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:27#2/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:27#2/r8.claim: If higher meanings hidden within plain religious teaching were exposed to everyone, all but a rare few would fail to bear them; God communicates according to each person’s understanding and capacity.
TABATABAI:42:27#2/r8.anchor: كلمهم في ذلك نوع تكليم يستفيد منه كل على قدر فهمه وسعة صدره كما قال في مثل ضربه في ذلك

TABATABAI:42:28-29/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:28-29/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:28-29/r1.claim: The rain-and-valleys parable in 13:17 illustrates how people receive higher meanings according to their capacities.
TABATABAI:42:28-29/r1.anchor: أنزل من السماء ماء فسالت أوديه بقدرها

TABATABAI:42:28-29/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:28-29/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:28-29/r2.claim: Religious duties are distributed according to people’s different trials; assigning every duty to everyone would burden them beyond what they could bear.
TABATABAI:42:28-29/r2.anchor: لو كلف بجميعها جميع الناس لتحرجوا منها ولم يتحملوها لكنه سبحانه قسمها بينهم حسب تقسيم الابتلاءات

TABATABAI:42:28-29/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:28-29/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:28-29/r3.claim: Religious knowledge and laws, like material provision, are allotted to people according to what will improve their condition.
TABATABAI:42:28-29/r3.anchor: فالرزق بالمعارف والشرائع من أي جهة فرض كالرزق الصوري مفروز بين الناس مقدر على حسب صلاح حالهم

TABRISI:42:26-27/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:42:26-27/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:42:26-27/r2.claim: If provision were expanded according to people's wishes, they would become arrogant, compete, dominate and oppress one another, and abandon obedience.
TABRISI:42:26-27/r2.anchor: لبطروا النعمة وتنافسوا وتغالبوا وظلموا في الأرض وتغلب بعضهم على بعض وخرجوا عن الطاعة

TABRISI:42:26-27/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:42:26-27/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:42:26-27/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains their transgression as continually seeking higher rank, better mounts, and finer clothing.
TABRISI:42:26-27/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس بغيهم في الأرض طلبهم منزلة بعد منزلة ودابة دابة وملبسا بعد ملبس

TABRISI:42:26-27/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:42:26-27/r4.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:42:26-27/r4.claim: Qatāda says God apportions provision in the measure that serves people's welfare.
TABRISI:42:26-27/r4.anchor: عن قتادة والمعنى أنه يوسع الرزق على من تكون مصلحته فيه

TABRISI:42:26-27/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:42:26-27/r5.speaker: أنس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن جبرائيل عن الله
TABRISI:42:26-27/r5.claim: A report from God through Gabriel and the Prophet, transmitted by Anas, says some servants need sickness, health, wealth, or poverty; their opposites would corrupt them, for God manages them knowing their hearts.
TABRISI:42:26-27/r5.anchor: الحديث الذي رواه أنس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن جبرائيل ع عن الله

TABRISI:42:26-27/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:42:26-27/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:42:26-27/r6.claim: In response to the objection that some wealthy people do transgress, the author says their conduct might have been just as bad or worse without the extra provision; God knows each case.
TABRISI:42:26-27/r6.anchor: قلنا إنا إذا علمنا على الجملة أنه سبحانه يدبر أمور عباده بحسب ما يعلم من مصالحهم

TABRISI:42:27-30/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:42:27-30/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:42:27-30/r1.claim: God knows people's circumstances and sees what benefits or harms them.
TABRISI:42:27-30/r1.anchor: عليم بأحوالهم بصير بما يصلحهم وما يفسدهم

THALABI:v8p317/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p317/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p317/r2.claim: The verse was revealed about people of the Suffa who wished for worldly plenty after seeing the wealth of Qurayza, Nadir, and Qaynuqa.
THALABI:v8p317/r2.anchor: الآية نزلت في قوم من أهل الصفة تمنوا سعة الدنيا والغنى

THALABI:v8p317/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p317/r3.speaker: خباب بن لادن
THALABI:v8p317/r3.claim: Khabbab says the verse concerned his group: they saw the wealth of Qurayza, Nadir, and Qaynuqa, desired it, and the verse was revealed.
THALABI:v8p317/r3.anchor: قال خباب بن لادن: فينا نزلت هذه الآية وذلك إنا نظرنا إلى بني قريظة والنضير وبني القينقاع، فتمنيناها

THALABI:v8p317/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p317/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p317/r4.claim: If God expanded everyone's provision, they would overstep bounds by rebelling and disobeying.
THALABI:v8p317/r4.anchor: لبغوا في الأرض أي لطغوا وعصوا

THALABI:v8p317/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p317/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v8p317/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas describes their transgression as escalating luxuries: one dwelling after another, mount, vehicle, and clothing after the next.
THALABI:v8p317/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: بغيهم ظلما، منزلة بعد منزلة ودابة بعد دابة ومركبا بعد مركب وملبسا بعد ملبس.

THALABI:v8p317/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p317/r6.speaker: شقيق بن إبراهيم
THALABI:v8p317/r6.claim: Shafiq says that if people were freed from work and livelihood by unearned wealth, they would rebel and spread corruption; keeping them occupied in earning a living is God's mercy and favor.
THALABI:v8p317/r6.anchor: قال: شقيق بن إبراهيم في قول الله تعالى:

THALABI:v8p317/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p317/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p317/r7.claim: God apportions each person's provision at the amount He wills, sufficient for their needs.
THALABI:v8p317/r7.anchor: ولكن ينزل بقدر ما يشاء أرزاقهم بقدر ما يشاء لكفايتهم

THALABI:v8p317/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p317/r8.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v8p317/r8.claim: Muqatil says God makes one person poor and another rich.
THALABI:v8p317/r8.anchor: قال مقاتل: ولكن ينزل بقدر ما يشاء فجعل واحدا فقيرا وآخرا غنيا.

THALABI:v8p317/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p317/r9.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v8p317/r9.claim: Qatada cites the maxim that the best provision is what neither makes a person transgress nor distracts them.
THALABI:v8p317/r9.anchor: قال قتادة: في هذه الآية كان يقال: خير الرزق ما لا يطغيك ولا يلهيك،

THALABI:v8p317/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p317/r10.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v8p317/r10.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says his greatest fear for the community was the flowering and abundance of worldly life.
THALABI:v8p317/r10.anchor: وذكر لنا إن نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «أخوف ما أخاف على أمتي، زهرة الدنيا وكثرتها

THALABI:v8p317/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p317/r11.speaker: الله عز وجل
THALABI:v8p317/r11.claim: In a divine report, God promises aid to His friends and says illness, health, wealth, poverty, and even modes of worship vary according to what will benefit each servant; He governs them knowing their hearts.
THALABI:v8p317/r11.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، عن جبريل (عليه السلام) ، عن ربه عز وجل قال: «من أهان لي وليا،

THALABI:v8p318/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p318/r1.speaker: صدقة
THALABI:v8p318/r1.claim: Sadaqa says he heard Aban ibn Abi Ayyash relate the divine report from Anas, then prayed not to be impoverished because he was among those whom only wealth would set right.
THALABI:v8p318/r1.anchor: قال صدقة: وسمعت أبان بن أبي عياش يحدث بهذا الحديث، عن أنس بن مالك ثم يقول: اللهم إني من عبادك المؤمنين

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:42:24-27/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:42:24-27/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:42:24-27/r6.claim: If God made provision abundant for all His servants, they would transgress and disobey; instead, He apportions it, making some poor and others rich, with knowledge and sight of His servants.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:42:24-27/r6.anchor: لطغوا وعصوا { ولكن ينزل بقدر ما يشاء } فيجعل واحدا فقيرا، وآخر غنيا

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:27/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:27/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:27/r1.claim: The verse addresses the difficult question of how worldly means are distributed and clarifies the preceding statement that God gives believers who do good more of His grace.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:27/r1.anchor: önceki âyette geçen Allah Teâlâ’nın iman edip iyi işler yapanlara kendi lutfundan fazlasını vermesine ilişkin ifadenin doğru anlaşılmasına ışık tutulmaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:27/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:27/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:27/r2.claim: If everyone received abundant and equal intelligence, health, ability, and wealth, social order, self-development, systematic work, and civilization would fail, leaving chaos.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:27/r2.anchor: Şayet Allah dünya hayatında herkese zekâ, sağlık, yetenek, servet vb. nimetleri bol ve eşit biçimde vermiş olsa, dirlik düzenlikten söz edilemez

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:27/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:27/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:27/r3.claim: Allocating livelihood according to who is good or bad would remove life's test, which is tied to humanity's purpose and to the purpose of life and death.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:27/r3.anchor: İyi ve kötü kriterine göre rızık verilmesi halinde ise insanın yaratılış amacı, hayatın ve ölümün var ediliş sebebi olan sınav ortamı teşekkül etmez

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:27/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:27/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:27/r4.claim: The verse explicitly answers that God, who fully knows and sees His servants' condition, distributes provision according to the measure He wills.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:27/r4.anchor: Kullarının durumunu çok iyi bilen ve gören yüce Allah rızkı kendi dilediği ölçüye göre vermektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:27/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:27/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:27/r5.claim: People cannot grasp this measure from their own perspective.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:27/r5.anchor: Kul planında bu ölçüyü idrak mümkün değildir;

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:27/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:27/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:27/r6.claim: A person's duty is to strive fully for means that bring well-being in this life and the next, and to use what is given as well as possible.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:27/r6.anchor: dünya ve âhiret mutluluğunu sağlayacak imkânları elde etmek için elinden gelen bütün çabayı harcamak ve verilenleri en iyi biçimde değerlendirmekle yükümlü

BURHAN:v3p100/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p100/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p100/r1.claim: God explains withholding abundant provision by the transgression it would cause among people.
BURHAN:v3p100/r1.anchor: ولو بسط الله الرزق لعباده لبغوا في الأرض

QUSHAYRI:v3p166/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p166/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p166/r4.claim: The verse sounds outwardly like a human apology: God did not expand a poor servant’s provision because He knew abundance would make the servant transgress and spread corruption.
QUSHAYRI:v3p166/r4.anchor: والمعنى أنني لم أبسط عليك أيها الفقير في الدنيا لما كان لي من العلم أنني لو قسمت عليك الدنيا لطغيت

QUSHAYRI:v3p166/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p166/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p166/r5.claim: The adversative “but” corrects the idea that God either grants all one wants or withholds everything: He apportions provision as He wills.
QUSHAYRI:v3p166/r5.anchor: ولم أمنع عنك ( الكل ) ؛ لأني أنزل بقدر ما أشاء

ITQAN:v1p52/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p52/r9.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p52/r9.claim: “If God were to expand provision” was revealed concerning the People of the Bench (Ahl al-Suffa).

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p24/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p24/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p24/r1.claim: A useful metaphor conveys an additional meaning through an underlying simile; its possible forms are too numerous for exhaustive treatment here.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p24/r1.anchor: وجملة تلك الفائدة وذلك الغرض التشبيه إلا أن طرقه تختلف حتى تفوت النهاية

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p24/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p24/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p24/r2.claim: Calling a brave man a lion intensifies the description and places the lion’s force, daring, and ferocity before the listener.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p24/r2.anchor: المبالغة في وصف المقصود بالشجاعة وإيقاعك منه في نفس السامع صورة الأسد في بطشه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p24/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p24/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p24/r3.claim: Calling someone a sea suggests generosity and openhandedness; sun and moon suggest beauty, radiance, and brilliance.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p24/r3.anchor: وهكذا أفدت باستعارة البحر سعته في الجود وفيض الكف وبالشمس والبدر ما لهما من الجمال

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p24/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p24/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p24/r4.claim: Calling a man a drawn sword can mean that he is forceful in supporting you or that his judgment is penetrating.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p24/r4.anchor: وسللت سيفا على العدو تريد رجلا ماضيا في نصرتك أو رأيا نافذا

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p24/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p24/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p24/r5.claim: Calling a human by the horse-specific al-mirsan adds no sense beyond saying nose, so this is not a meaningful metaphor; useful metaphorical simile is shared across languages.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p24/r5.anchor: اختصاص المرسن بغير الآدمي لا يفيد أكثر مما يفيده الأنف في الآدمي

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p375/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p375/r1.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p375/r1.claim: Khabbab says the verse came down about the People of the Bench, who saw the wealth of Qurayza and Nadir and wished they had it.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p375/r1.anchor: قال خباب بن الأرت: فينا نزلت هذه الآية، وذلك أنا نظرنا إلى أموال قريظة

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p375/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p375/r2.speaker: عمرو بن حريث
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p375/r2.claim: Amr ibn Hurayth likewise says the verse concerned the People of the Bench, who wished they had worldly riches.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p375/r2.anchor: أخبرني أبو هانئ الخولاني أنه سمع عمرو بن حريث يقول: إنما نزلت هذه الآية في أصحاب الصفة

DAMGHANI:v1p67/r11.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p67/r11.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p67/r11.claim: Basṭ means expansion or abundance; God expands provision for whom He wills.
DAMGHANI:v1p67/r11.anchor: أي وسع . كقوله تعالى في سورة الرعد

DAMGHANI:v1p453/r8.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p453/r8.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p453/r8.claim: Yunazzilu can mean to distribute or expand provision in measured amounts.
DAMGHANI:v1p453/r8.anchor: الثامن الإنزال البسط قوله تعالى في سورة حم عسق ولو بسط الله الرزق لعباده لبغوا في الأرض ولكن ينزل بقدر ما يشاء

NAHHAS:v4p81/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p81/r6.speaker: الخليل
NAHHAS:v4p81/r6.claim: Al-Khalīl permits sīn to shift to ṣād before ṭāʾ because the sounds are close, relevant to بسط.
NAHHAS:v4p81/r6.anchor: وأجاز الخليل رحمه الله في السين إذا كانت بعدها طاء أن تقلب صادا لقربها منها

ASAD-NOTES:42:27#n31/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:42:27#n31/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:42:27#n31/r1.claim: Asad connects this verse to 42:26: its promise that God responds to believers seems at odds with wrongdoers prospering while righteous people suffer in this life.
ASAD-NOTES:42:27#n31/r1.anchor: This passage connects with, and elucidates, the statement in the preceding verse

ASAD-NOTES:42:27#n31/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:42:27#n31/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:42:27#n31/r2.claim: The verse elliptically points to human greed for more and the arrogance of those who imagine themselves self-sufficient.
ASAD-NOTES:42:27#n31/r2.anchor: man's innate "greed for mere and more" (see 102:1), which often causes him to become "grossly overweening whenever he believes himself to be self-sufficient" (96:6).

ASAD-NOTES:42:27#n31/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:42:27#n31/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:42:27#n31/r3.claim: God's response to both righteous people and wrongdoers becomes fully evident in the hereafter, not necessarily in this world, which is only life's short first stage.
ASAD-NOTES:42:27#n31/r3.anchor: God's "response" to the righteous - as well as to wrongdoers - will become fully evident only in the life to come

QIRAAT-ER:42:27:14#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:42:27:14#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:42:27:14#1/r1.claim: The Form IV variant is a simpler causative sending-down; Form II can suggest staged or intensive descent, though both mean causing descent.
QIRAAT-ER:42:27:14#1/r1.anchor: Canonical variant reads Form IV instead of Form II; both mean causing descent

ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#2/r1.claim: If God expanded provision, people would grow arrogant and exceed the limits fitting for servants, or wrong one another; wealth readily breeds insolence and pride.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#2/r1.anchor: أي لتكبروا فيها بطرا وتجاوز الحد الذي يليق بالعبيد أو لظلم بعضهم بعضا فإن الغني مبطرة مأشرة

ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#2/r2.claim: A hadith says the Prophet most feared worldly abundance and its increase for his community.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#2/r2.anchor: وفي الحديث أخوف ما أخاف على أمتي زهرة الدنيا وكثرتها

ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#2/r3.claim: An Arab poetic line about the wasmi rain growing plants precedes the gloss that baghy is seeking more than one's due, in amount or quality.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#2/r3.anchor: ولبعض العرب : وقد جعل الوسمي ينبت بيننا وبين بني روماننبعاوشوحطا وأصلا لبغي طلب أكثر مما يجب

ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#2/r4.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#2/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read yunazzilu without doubling, from anzala; the majority read it doubled.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو بالتخفيف من الأنزال

ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#2/r5.claim: Bi-qadar means by a measured determination of what God's wisdom requires.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#2/r5.anchor: بقدر ( بتقدير ( ما يشاء ( وهوما اقتضته حكمته جل شأنه

ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r1.claim: God knows servants' hidden and manifest circumstances and apportions each person's provision at each time as befits them, withholding or giving, contracting or expanding, in accord with divine wisdom.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r1.anchor: محيط بخفيات أمورهم وجلاياها فيقدر لكل واحدمنهم فيكل وقت من أوقاتهم ما يليق بشأنه

ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r2.claim: Universal enrichment would bring transgression, while universal poverty would bring ruin; either extreme disrupts the order of the world.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r2.anchor: ولو أغناهم جميعا لبغوا ولو أفقرهم لهلكوا

ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r3.claim: An objection says poverty too can cause transgression, so the verse's conditional relation is not self-evident.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r3.anchor: واستشكلت الآية بأن الغنى كما يكون سبب البغي فذلك الفقر قد يكون فلا يظهر الشرطية

ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r4.speaker: جار الله
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r4.claim: Jar Allah answers that transgression is less likely under poverty and more likely under abundance; if abundance were universal, transgression would predominate and reverse the present order.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r4.anchor: وأجاب جار الله بأنه لا شبهة أن البغي مع الفقر أقل ومع البسط أكثر

ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r5.claim: The author explains that the current mixed distribution checks wrongdoing: fear of the poor restrains the rich, while the poor's greater dependence on the rich encourages cooperation and curbs their own excess.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r5.anchor: وأما الذي عليه سنة الله عز وجل فهو الذي جمع الأمرين مشتملا على خوف للغني من الفقراء يزعه عن الظلم

ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r6.speaker: صاحب الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r6.claim: The author endorses the Kashf explanation as a sound answer without forced reasoning and uses it to reject al-Tibi's criticism that the objection is strong and its answer strained.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r6.anchor: كذا قرره صاحب الكشف ثم قال : وهذا جواب حسن لا تكلف فيه وهو إشارة إلى رد العلامة الطيبي

ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r7.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r7.claim: Al-Tibi takes ʿibādihi here as servants specially honored by God and made His friends; the closing words indicate God's knowledge of their circumstances and what benefits or harms them.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r7.anchor: وذهب هو إلى أن المراد ( بعباده ) من خصهم الله تعالى بالكرامة وجعلهم من أوليائه

ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r8.claim: A report says that when God loves a servant, He protects him from worldly life as one protects a sick person from water.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r8.anchor: إذاأحب الله تعالى عبداحماه الدنياكمايظل أحدكم يحمي سقيمه الماء

ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r9.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r9.claim: Khabbab said they saw the wealth of Qurayza, Nadir, and Qaynuqa and wished for it; the verse was then revealed.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r9.anchor: ويشد من عضده قولخباب بن الأرت نظرناإلى أموال بني قريظة والنضير وبنيقينقاعفتمنيناها فنزلت

ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r10.speaker: عمرو بن حريث
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r10.claim: Amr ibn Hurayth says people of the Suffa asked the Messenger to enrich them and expand their provision, after which the verse was revealed.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r10.anchor: وقول عمرو ابنحريث طلب قوم من أهل الصفة من الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يغنيهمالله تعالى ويبسط لهم الأموال والأرزاقفنزلت

ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r11.speaker: محيي السنة
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r11.claim: The interpretation that the servants singled out are God's honored friends is also attributed to Muhyi al-Sunna.

ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r12.claim: The author finds the general explanation more fitting, since God's elect are unlikely to be intoxicated by wealth; alternatively, the warning can concern some believing servants.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p38#3/r12.anchor: فلعل الأولى ما تقدمأو يقال : إن هذا في بعض العباد المؤمنين فتأمل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p194/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p194/r5.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p194/r5.claim: Khabbāb ibn al-Aratt says the verse was revealed about them: they saw the wealth of Banū Qurayẓa, Banū al-Naḍīr, and Banū Qaynuqāʿ and wished for it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p194/r5.anchor: قال خباب بن الأرت: فينا نزلت هذه الآية، وذلك أنا نظرنا إلى أموال بني قريظة وبني النضير وبني قينقاع فتمنيناها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p194/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p194/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p194/r6.claim: Baghaw means they would become tyrannical and insolent on earth.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p194/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p194/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p194/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās describes their transgression as seeking one status after another, one mount after another, and one kind of clothing after another.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p194/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس: بغيهم طلبهم منزلة بعد منزلة ومركبا بعد مركب وملبسا بعد ملبس

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p194/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p194/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p194/r8.claim: God apportions people's provision as He wills, in consideration of His servants; He knows and sees them.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p194/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p194/r9.speaker: أنس بن مالك عن النبي عن جبريل عن الله
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p194/r9.claim: In a divine report, God says whoever humiliates His ally wages war on Him; He loves obligatory acts and then voluntary acts, answers the loved servant's prayers, and gives some servants wealth or poverty because that condition preserves their faith. The segment's report ends mid-sentence; no grading is stated.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p194/r9.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن جبريل عن الله عز وجل قال

BAYDAWI-FULL:42:26-27/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:26-27/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:26-27/r7.claim: If provision were expanded, people would grow arrogant and corrupt through excess; alternatively, some would dominate and oppress others. This describes the prevalent pattern.
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:26-27/r7.anchor: لتكبروا وأفسدوا فيها بطرا، أو لبغى بعضهم على بعض استيلاء واستعلاء وهذا على الغالب

BAYDAWI-FULL:42:26-27/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:26-27/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:26-27/r8.claim: The root baghy means seeking to go beyond moderation in the quantity or quality of what one pursues.
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:26-27/r8.anchor: وأصل البغي طلب تجاوز الاقتصاد فيما يتحرى كمية أو كيفية

BAYDAWI-FULL:42:26-27/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:26-27/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:26-27/r9.claim: God measures provision according to His will and knowledge of people's hidden and evident states, allotting what suits their circumstances.
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:26-27/r9.anchor: يعلم خفايا أمرهم وجلايا حالهم فيقدر لهم ما يناسب شأنهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:42:26-27/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:26-27/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:26-27/r10.claim: One report says the verse came down after the People of the Bench wished for wealth.
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:26-27/r10.anchor: روي أن أهل الصفة تمنوا الغنى فنزلت

BAYDAWI-FULL:42:26-27/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:26-27/r11.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:26-27/r11.claim: Another report says Arabs would fight when conditions were fertile and migrate in search of pasture during drought.
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:26-27/r11.anchor: وقيل في العرب كانوا إذا أخصبوا تحاربوا وإذا أجدبوا انتجعوا

BIQAI-FULL:v6p628/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p628/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p628/r3.claim: Divine response does not mean granting every worldly request as specified: abundant grants often breed arrogance and misery, defeating the supplicant's purpose.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p628/r3.anchor: الإجابة إلى كل ما يسأل بأن يكون في هذه الدار يؤدي في الغالب إلى البطر

BIQAI-FULL:v6p628/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p628/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p628/r4.claim: A hadith says a prayer may be answered by granting the request, averting a comparable affliction, or deferring its reward to the Hereafter; the author gives no transmitter or grading.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p628/r4.anchor: وتارة تكون بدفع مثله من البلاء

BIQAI-FULL:v6p628/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p628/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p628/r5.claim: The divine name emphasizes the greatness of the matter, which requires full knowledge of human traits and the power to give or withhold.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p628/r5.anchor: أي الملك الأعظم الجامع لجميع صفات الكمال

BIQAI-FULL:v6p628/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p628/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p628/r6.claim: If God gave all servants, repentant and otherwise, more than they needed, they would pursue every desire by force like powerful kings, multiplying killing, plunder, and other corruption.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p628/r6.anchor: أي لصاروا يريدون كل ما يشتهونه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p628/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p628/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p628/r7.claim: God apportions provision for people collectively and individually, not exceeding or falling short of the measure He sets, according to His wisdom.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p628/r7.anchor: أي بتقدير لهم جملة ولكل واحد منهم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p629/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p629/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p629/r1.claim: The wording encompasses all servants, not just those made wealthy or constrained; God knows their outward and inward states and arranges each person's situation and its causes accordingly.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p629/r1.anchor: يعلم جميع ظواهر أمورهم وحركاتهم وانتقالاتهم وكلامهم وبواطنها

DURR-FULL:v7p352/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p352/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v7p352/r1.claim: The verse is explained by people wishing for worldly life and saying, “If only we had [wealth].”
DURR-FULL:v7p352/r1.anchor: وذلك أنهم قالوا: لو أن لنا فتمنوا الدنيا

DURR-FULL:v7p352/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p352/r2.speaker: علي
DURR-FULL:v7p352/r2.claim: Ali says the verse was revealed about the people of the Ṣuffa, who wished for worldly wealth; al-Ḥākim authenticated the report.
DURR-FULL:v7p352/r2.anchor: عن علي رضي الله عنه قال: إنما أنزلت هذه الآية في أصحاب الصفة

DURR-FULL:v7p352/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p352/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p352/r3.claim: Qatāda says the best provision is what neither makes a person transgress nor distracts him.
DURR-FULL:v7p352/r3.anchor: عن قتادة في الآية قال: يقال خير الرزق ما لا يطغيك ولا يلهيك

DURR-FULL:v7p352/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p352/r4.speaker: رسول الله
DURR-FULL:v7p352/r4.claim: A prophetic report relayed by Qatāda says the Prophet most feared worldly bloom and adornment; after a question about good bringing evil, this verse was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v7p352/r4.anchor: ذكر لنا أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: أخوف ما أخاف على أمتي زهرة الدنيا وزخرفها

DURR-FULL:v7p352/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p352/r5.speaker: رسول الله
DURR-FULL:v7p352/r5.claim: The Prophet answers that good only brings good, while luxuriant growth may overwhelm and kill an animal that gorges on it.
DURR-FULL:v7p352/r5.anchor: إن الخير لا يأتي إلا بالخير ولكنه والله ما كان ربيع قط إلا أحبط أو ألم

DURR-FULL:v7p352/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p352/r6.speaker: رسول الله
DURR-FULL:v7p352/r6.claim: The report contrasts wealth spent in God's prescribed, approved path with wealth spent on lusts while withholding God's due; the former is intended for good, the latter for evil.
DURR-FULL:v7p352/r6.anchor: فأما عبد أعطاه الله مالا فوضعه في سبيل الله التي افترض وارتضى

DURR-FULL:v7p352/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p352/r7.speaker: رسول الله
DURR-FULL:v7p352/r7.claim: Abū Saʿīd's prophetic report warns of worldly wealth, says good does not bring evil, and praises a Muslim who uses wealth for kinship and God's path; wrongful acquisition leaves its owner unsatisfied and testifies against him.
DURR-FULL:v7p352/r7.anchor: عن أبي سعيد رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: إن أخوف ما أخاف عليكم ما يخرج الله لكم من زهرة الدنيا

DURR-FULL:v7p353/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p353/r1.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p353/r1.claim: Qatāda says the best life is what does not make a person transgress or distract him.
DURR-FULL:v7p353/r1.anchor: عن قتادة {ولو بسط الله الرزق لعباده لبغوا في الأرض} قال: كان يقال خير العيش ما لا يطغيك ولا يلهيك

DURR-FULL:v7p353/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p353/r2.speaker: الله
DURR-FULL:v7p353/r2.claim: In a divine report, God says that harming one of His friends is declaring war on Him, and that He is fiercely protective of His friends.
DURR-FULL:v7p353/r2.anchor: عن أنس رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن جبريل عن الله عز وجل قال: يقول الله عز وجل: من أهان لي وليا فقد بارزني بالمحاربة

DURR-FULL:v7p353/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p353/r3.speaker: الله
DURR-FULL:v7p353/r3.claim: The report says the most beloved approach to God is performing obligations, followed by voluntary worship; God then becomes the beloved servant’s hearing, sight, hand, and support, answering prayer and granting requests.
DURR-FULL:v7p353/r3.anchor: وما تقرب إلي عبدي المؤمن بمثل أداء ما افترضت عليه وما يزال عبدي المؤمن يتقرب إلي بالنوافل حتى أحبه

DURR-FULL:v7p353/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p353/r4.speaker: الله
DURR-FULL:v7p353/r4.claim: God’s reported hesitation concerns taking the soul of a believing servant who dislikes death, though death is inevitable and God dislikes causing him distress.
DURR-FULL:v7p353/r4.anchor: وما ترددت في شيء أنا فاعله ترددي في قبض روح عبدي المؤمن يكره الموت وأكره مساءته

DURR-FULL:v7p353/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p353/r5.speaker: الله
DURR-FULL:v7p353/r5.claim: God may withhold some worship, health, or sickness from a servant because it would corrupt that person’s faith; He says He orders affairs by knowing hearts.
DURR-FULL:v7p353/r5.anchor: وإن من عبادي المؤمنين لمن يسألني الباب من العبادة فأكفه عنه أن لا يدخله عجب فيفسده ذلك

DURR-FULL:v7p353/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p353/r6.speaker: الله
DURR-FULL:v7p353/r6.claim: The divine report closes by grounding God's management of servants' affairs in His knowledge of their hearts and naming Him all-knowing and aware.
DURR-FULL:v7p353/r6.anchor: إني أدبر أمر عبادي بعلمي بقلوبهم إني عليم خبير

DURR-FULL:v7p353/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p353/r7.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p353/r7.claim: Mujāhid glosses the provision in the verse as rain.
DURR-FULL:v7p353/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله {ولو بسط الله الرزق لعباده لبغوا} قال: المطر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r1.speaker: مقاتل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r1.claim: Muqatil excludes the passage from verse 23 through verse 24 from the otherwise Meccan surah; it is said to have been revealed about the Ansar and is among Ibn Abbas's four cited verses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r1.anchor: وعن مقاتل استثناء قوله تعالى : { ذلك الذي يبشر الله عباده الذين آمنوا إلى قوله : إنه عليم بذات الصدور }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r2.speaker: مقاتل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r2.claim: According to Muqatil as quoted in Ibn al-Faras's Ahkam al-Qurʾan, verse 27 was revealed about the People of the Bench, making it Medinan.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r2.anchor: وفي ( أحكام القرآن ) لابن الفرس عن مقاتل : أن قوله تعالى : { ولو بسط الله الرزق لعباده }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r3.speaker: مقاتل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r3.claim: Muqatil also says the passage in verses 39–41 about responding to aggression was revealed in Medina.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r3.anchor: وفيه عنه أن قوله تعالى : { والذين إذا أصابهم البغي هم ينتصرون إلى قوله : ما عليهم من سبيل }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r4.speaker: الجعبري عن جابر بن زيد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r4.claim: In the order attributed by al-Jaʿbari from Jabir ibn Zayd, the surah followed al-Kahf and preceded Ibrahim, and was the sixty-ninth revealed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r4.anchor: وعدت التاسعة والستين في ترتيب نزول السور عند الجعبري المروي عن جابر بن زيد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAshur suggests revelation may have continued into year nine, after the Aqaba pledge, because the Ansar could be intended in verse 38 even before the Hijra.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r6.anchor: ولعل نزولها استمر إلى سنة تسع بعد أن آمن نقباء الأنصار ليلة العقبة فقد قيل : إن قوله : { والذين استجابوا لربهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r7.claim: Madinan, Meccan, Syrian, and Basran verse counts give the surah fifty verses, while the Kufan count gives fifty-three.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r7.anchor: وعدت آيها عند أهل المدينة ومكة والشام والبصرة خمسين ، وعند أهل الكوفة ثلاثا وخمسين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r8.claim: The surah challenges those who deny revelation to produce speech like the Quran, a challenge common to surahs opened by disjointed letters, as in al-Baqara.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r8.anchor: أول أغراضها الإشارة إلى تحدي الطاعنين في أن القرآن وحي من الله بأن يأتوا بكلام مثله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r9.claim: God argues that Muhammad's revelation resembles that given to earlier messengers and warns Mecca and its surroundings of Judgment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r9.anchor: واستدل الله على المعاندين بأن الوحي إلى محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ما هو إلا كالوحي إلى الرسل من قبله لينذر أهل مكة ومن حولها بيوم الحساب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r10.claim: God owns the heavens and earth, whose realms submit to Him; as creator of beings, He chooses messengers and may legislate for this community as for earlier ones.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r10.anchor: وأن الله الذي له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض لا تعارض قدرته ولا يشك في حكمته ، وقد خضعت له العوالم العليا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r11.claim: All messengers sent to address people generally were human recipients of revelation; God had not previously sent angels to address the masses directly.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r11.anchor: وما أرسل الله الرسل إلا من البشر يوحي إليهم فلم يسبق أن أرسل ملائكة لمخاطبة عموم الناس مباشرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r12.claim: The polytheists have no proof beyond imitating leaders of disbelief who instituted idolatry and planted doubts among them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r12.anchor: وأن المشركين بالله لا حجة لهم إلا تقليد أيمة الكفر الذين شرعوا لهم الإشراك وألقوا إليهم الشبهات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r13.claim: The surah warns of Judgment and the approaching Hour, describing idolaters' punishment while alluding to believers' honor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r13.anchor: وحذرهم يوم الجزاء واقتراب الساعة وما سيلقى المشركون يوم الحساب من العذاب مع إدماج التعريض بالترغيب فيما سيلقاه المؤمنون من الكرامة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r14.claim: Reflection shows that the Prophet does not invent claims about God, since God would not allow him to attribute words falsely to Him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r14.anchor: وأنهم لو تدبروا لعلموا أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يأتي عن الله من تلقاء نفسه لأن الله لا يقره على أن يقول عليه ما لم يقله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r15.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r15.claim: The surah presents signs of divine unity, including blessings such as navigation at sea and worldly provisions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r15.anchor: وذكرت دلائل الوحدانية وما هو من تلك الآيات نعمة على الناس مثل دليل السير في البحر وما أوتيه الناس من نعم الدنيا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p72/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p72/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p72/r1.claim: The preceding scholarly disagreement is, in Ibn ʿAshur's view, verbal and built on technical terminology and fine distinctions among schools; no one disputes God's beneficence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p72/r1.anchor: هذه مسألة أرجع المحققون الخلاف فيها إلى اللفظ والبناء على المصطلحات والاعتبارات الموافقة لدقائق المذاهب ، إذ لا ينازع أحد في نعمة المنعمين منهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p72/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p72/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p72/r2.claim: The phrase He is the Powerful, the Mighty may modify the attribute لطيف or the sentence that He provides whom He wills.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p72/r2.anchor: وعطف { وهو القوي العزيز } على صفة { لطيف } أو على جملة { يرزق من يشاء }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p72/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p72/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p72/r3.claim: Calling God powerful and mighty prevents imagining His gentleness as weakness or accommodation, and His giving as stinginess or scarcity; His distribution follows wisdom about His creatures.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p72/r3.anchor: ويفيد الاحتراس من توهم أن لطفه عن عجز أو مصانعة ، فإنه قوي عزيز لا يعجز ولا يصانع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p72/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p72/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p72/r4.claim: The definite predicate makes strength and might exclusive to God in an emphatic generic sense, as though others' power and dignity were nonexistent.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p72/r4.anchor: والإخبار عن اسم الجلالة بالمسند المعرفف باللام يفيد معنى قصر القوة والعزة عليه تعالى ، وهو قصر الجنس للمبالغة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p72/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p72/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p72/r5.claim: This passage connects to verse 18's contrast: believers focus on the afterlife, while unbelievers' concerns stop at worldly life; the present passage details God's differing treatment of the two groups.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p72/r5.anchor: هذه الآية متصلة بقوله : { يستعجل بها الذين لا يؤمنون بها والذين آمنوا مشفقون منها } ( الشورى : 18 ) الآية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p72/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p72/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p72/r6.claim: The clauses concerning God's gentleness and His differentiated treatment are left without conjunction because they are closely connected to the contrast in verse 18 and to the preceding preamble in verse 19.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p72/r6.anchor: ولأجل هذا الاتصال بينها وبين جملة يستعجل بها الذين لا يؤمنون بها } ( الشورى : 18 ) ترك عطفها عليها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p92/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p92/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p92/r1.claim: Addressing all God's servants makes the statement universal; this yields a general wisdom for the cosmic order and serves as a conclusive coda.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p92/r1.anchor: وقد وردت هذه الآية موردا كليا لأن قوله { لعباده } يعم جميع العباد . ومن هذه الكلية تحصل فائدة المسؤول عليه الجزئي الخاص بالمؤمنين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p92/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p92/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p92/r2.claim: The world runs by general laws, not a separate worldly system reserved for God's allies; their special gifts are nearness, divine approval, and eternal success, though some may be singled out to establish truth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p92/r2.anchor: أي أن الله أسس نظام هذا العالم على قوانين عامة وليس من حكمته أن يخص أولياءه وحزبه بنظام تكويني دنيوي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p92/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p92/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p92/r3.claim: Baghy means aggression and injustice: wealth can provoke insolence and oppression when it meets a corrupt character.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p92/r3.anchor: والبغي : العدوان والظلم ، أي لبغى بعضهم على بعض لأن الغنى مظنة البطر والأشر إذا صادف نفسا خبيثة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p92/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p92/r4.speaker: بعض بني جرم من طيء
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p92/r4.claim: A poet of Banu Jarm from Tayy illustrates that abundance can make people hostile, whereas drought makes them dependent.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p92/r4.anchor: قال بعض بني جرم من طيء من شعراء الحماسة : إذا أخصبتمو كنتم عدوا وإن أجدبتمو كنتم عيالا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p92/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p92/r5.speaker: بعض العرب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p92/r5.claim: A second Arab poem, quoted in al-Kashshaf, describes winter rain causing valuable trees to grow between the speaker's people and Banu Ruman as an illustration in the discussion of oppression.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p92/r5.anchor: ولبعض العرب أنشده في ( الكشاف ) : وقد جعل الوسمي ينبت بيننا وبين بني رومان نبعا وشوحطا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p92/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p92/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p92/r6.claim: Poverty seldom causes oppression, except rarely when fear is involved, as when a starving person uses force to escape; that exceptional case is not the verse's focus.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p92/r6.anchor: فأما الفقر فقلما كان سببا للبغي إلا بغيا مشوبا بمخافة كبغي الجائع بالافتكاك بالعنف فذلك لندرته لا يلتفت إليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p92/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p92/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p92/r7.claim: The verse explains why provision is measured, not why poverty exists.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p92/r7.anchor: على أن السياق لبيان حكمة كون الرزق بقدر لا لبيان حكمة في الفقر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p92/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p92/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p92/r8.claim: The conditional and answer remain causally linked even though the opposite condition can sometimes cause oppression too; provision includes intermediate degrees from sufficiency to scarcity, hardship, and poverty.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p92/r8.anchor: فالتلازم بين الشرط وجوابه في قوله : { ولو بسط الله الرزق لعباده لبغوا } حاصل بهذه السببية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p92/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p92/r9.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p92/r9.claim: Khabbab reportedly said the verse came down about his group after they saw the wealth of Banu Nadir, Qurayza, and Qaynuqa and wished for it; Ibn ʿAshur treats this, if authentic, as Khabbab's interpretation and notes the verse is Meccan.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p92/r9.anchor: وعن خباب بن الأرت ( فينا نزلت هذه الآية ، وذلك أنا نظرنا إلى أموال بني النضير وبني قريظة وبني قينقاع فتمنيناها فنزلت )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p92/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p92/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p92/r10.claim: If authentic, Khabbab's statement is an interpretation rather than an occasion of revelation: the verse is Meccan, and he may have heard others apply it to their wish for wealth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p92/r10.anchor: وهذا إن صح عن خباب فهو تأويل منه لأن الآية مكية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p92/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p92/r11.speaker: أهل الصفة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p92/r11.claim: Another report says the verse was revealed about the People of the Bench, who wished for ample provision; Ibn ʿAshur grades this report weak.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p92/r11.anchor: وروي أنها نزلت في أهل الصفة تمنوا سعة الرزق فنزلت ، وهذا خبر ضعيف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p93/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p93/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p93/r1.claim: If everyone were affluent, the social order would collapse: some wealthy people would oppress others, victims would resist, and the cycle would produce widespread disorder.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p93/r1.anchor: لو جعل الله جميع الناس في بسطة من الرزق لاختل نظام حياتهم ببغي بعضهم على بعض لأن بعضهم الأغنياء تحدثه نفسه بالبغي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p93/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p93/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p93/r2.claim: Affluence given to some does not create this general corruption: a good character or religious restraint can prevent oppression, and harms by the unrestrained are rare and checked by law, courts, and communal zeal.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p93/r2.anchor: وبهذا تعلم أن بسط الرزق لبعض العباد كما هو مشاهد لا يفضي إلى مثل هذا الفساد لأن الغنى قد يصادف نفسا صالحة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p93/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p93/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p93/r3.claim: Using the verb anzala for giving provision is metaphorical: a gift from exalted God is pictured as descending from above, an expression repeated in the Quran.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p93/r3.anchor: وإطلاق فعل التنزيل على إعطاء الرزق في قوله تعالى : { ولكن ينزل بقدر } استعارة لأنه عطاء من رفيع الشأن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p93/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p93/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p93/r4.claim: Qadar, with fatḥa on both consonants, means measure or specification.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p93/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p93/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p93/r5.claim: God's will follows His knowledge and the causes He arranges for the different welfare of His creatures, including their competing interests; only He encompasses these determinations.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p93/r5.anchor: ومعنى { ما يشاء } أن مشيئته تعالى جارية على وفق علمه وعلى ما ييسره له من ترتيب الأسباب على حسب مختلف صالح مخلوقاته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p93/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p93/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p93/r6.claim: The closing statement that God knows and sees His servants explains the measured distribution of provision.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p93/r6.anchor: وكلها تدخل تحت قوله { إنه بعباده خبير بصير } ، وهي جملة واقعة موقع التعليل للتي قبلها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p93/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p93/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p93/r7.claim: Here inna does not emphasize truth; it draws attention and signals causation, functioning like fa and making the clause equivalent to a causal conjunct.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p93/r7.anchor: وافتتحت ب ( إن ) التي لم يرد منها تأكيد الخبر ولكنها لمجرد الاهتمام بالخبر والإيذان بالتعليل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p93/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p93/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p93/r8.claim: Khabir denotes knowledge of servants' interests and conditions before their causes are set in motion; basir denotes knowledge of their realized conditions, two relations of divine knowledge.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p93/r8.anchor: قبل تقديرها وتقدير أسبابها ، أي العلم بما سيكون . ووصف { بصير } دال على العلم المتعلق بأحوالهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p287/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p287/r1.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p287/r1.claim: Khabbab ibn al-Aratt says the provision verse came about his group, who saw the wealth of Banu Qurayza and Banu Nadir and wished for it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p287/r1.anchor: قال خباب بن الأرت فينا نزلت هذه الآية وذلك أنا نظرنا إلى أموال بني قريظة والنضير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p287/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p287/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p287/r2.claim: If God widened provision for everyone, they would grow insolent, disobey, and transgress against one another.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p287/r2.anchor: لو أوسع الله الرزق لعباده لبطروا وعصوا وبغى بعضهم على بعض

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p287/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p287/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p287/r3.claim: God apportions provision as suits people's circumstances and keeps them from becoming tyrannical.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p287/r3.anchor: أي ينزل أمره بتقدير ما يشاء مما يصلح أمورهم ولا يطغيهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p287/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p287/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p287/r4.claim: Some servants are improved only by wealth, and others only by poverty.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p287/r4.anchor: فمنهم من لا يصلحه إلا الغنى ومنهم من لا يصلحه إلا الفقر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p206/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p206/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p206/r2.claim: If people received more provision than they needed, some would oppress others out of arrogance and ingratitude.
