IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p206/r2.anchor: لو أعطاهم فوق حاجتهم من الرزق، لحملهم ذلك على البغي والطغيان من بعضهم على بعض

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p206/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p206/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p206/r3.claim: Qatadah cites the maxim that the best livelihood is one that neither distracts a person nor makes him transgress.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p206/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة: كان يقال: خير العيش ما لا يلهيك ولا يطغيك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p206/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p206/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p206/r4.claim: Qatadah also recalls the Prophet’s fear of worldly splendor and the question whether good can bring evil.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p206/r4.anchor: قتادة حديث: "إنما أخاف عليكم ما يخرج الله من زهرة الحياة الدنيا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p206/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p206/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p206/r5.claim: God chooses the amount of provision that benefits each person: He enriches whomever is suited to wealth and impoverishes whomever is suited to poverty.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p206/r5.anchor: يرزقهم من الرزق ما يختاره مما فيه صلاحهم، وهو أعلم بذلك فيغني من يستحق الغنى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p206/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p206/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p206/r6.claim: A report cited in support says some servants are helped only by wealth, while others are helped only by poverty, and the opposite condition would corrupt their religion.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p206/r6.anchor: إن من عبادي لمن (7) لا يصلحه إلا الغنى، ولو أفقرته لأفسدت عليه دينه

JISHUMI:v9p6246/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6246/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6246/r12.claim: Baghy means seeking an increase, and its root sense is seeking.
JISHUMI:v9p6246/r12.anchor: والبغي: طلب الزيادة، وأصله من الطلب

JISHUMI:v9p6247/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6247/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6247/r6.claim: Khabīr is the predicate of inna, whose pronoun is its subject.
JISHUMI:v9p6247/r6.anchor: (خبير) رفع؛ لأنه خبر (إن)، واسمها الهاء في (إنه)

JISHUMI:v9p6247/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6247/r9.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v9p6247/r9.claim: One account says the verse was revealed about some of the people of the Ṣuffa who wished for wealth and worldly abundance.
JISHUMI:v9p6247/r9.anchor: قيل: قوله: (ولو بسط الله الرزق) الآية نزلت في قوم من أهل الصفة، تمنوا الغنى وسعة الدنيا

JISHUMI:v9p6247/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6247/r10.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
JISHUMI:v9p6247/r10.claim: Khabbāb says the verse was revealed about them after they coveted the wealth of Qurayẓa, Naḍīr, and Banū Qaynuqāʿ.
JISHUMI:v9p6247/r10.anchor: وعن خباب بن الأرت: نزلت فينا هذه الآية، وذلك أنا نظرنا في أموال قريظة والنضير وبني قينقاع

JISHUMI:v9p6247/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6247/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6247/r11.claim: After warning the disobedient, the passage promises believers; pairing promise with warning is God's usual way of encouraging and deterring.
JISHUMI:v9p6247/r11.anchor: لما تقدم وعيد أهل العصيان عقبه بوعد المؤمنين على عادته تعالى بالجمع بين الوعد والوعيد ترغيبا وترهيبا

JISHUMI:v9p6253/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6253/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6253/r5.claim: God limits provision as لطف, giving people what brings them nearer to uprightness; His knowledge and sight show this serves their welfare in moral responsibility, not inability or stinginess.
JISHUMI:v9p6253/r5.anchor: وإنما رزقهم قدرا مخصوصا ليكونوا أقرب إلى الاستقامة؛ ولذلك عقبه بقوله: (إنه بعباده خبير بصير)

JISHUMI:v9p6253/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6253/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6253/r6.claim: The verse shows human acts arise from human agents: God widens or restricts provision to guide people toward obedience and away from sin.
JISHUMI:v9p6253/r6.anchor: أنه تعالى وسع وضيق لطفا؛ كي يكونوا أقرب إلي الطاعة، وأبعد من المعصية

JISHUMI:v9p6253/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6253/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6253/r7.claim: If God created all human acts, the distinction between widening and restricting provision would be pointless, since conduct would simply follow what He created.
JISHUMI:v9p6253/r7.anchor: فلو كان الجميع خلقا له - تعالى - لم يكن لهذا الكلام معنى؛ لأنه سواء وسع أو ضيق

JISHUMI:v9p6253/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6253/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6253/r8.claim: Ability is not the cause that compels rebellion or its absence; otherwise provision's abundance or scarcity would be irrelevant to whether rebellion occurs.
JISHUMI:v9p6253/r8.anchor: أن القدرة لو كانت موجبة لوقف وجود البغي وعدمه عليها، لا على سعة الرزق وضيقه، فتبطل فائدة الكلام

JISHUMI:v9p6253/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6253/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6253/r9.claim: Divine لطف presupposes that a person can perform either course; otherwise there is no point in calling provision's increase or decrease a لطف.
JISHUMI:v9p6253/r9.anchor: أن اللطف إنما يصح إذا قدر العبد على الفعلين، فأما إذا لم يقدر إلا على شيء بعينه

JISHUMI:v9p6253/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6253/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6253/r10.claim: God did not will rebellion for those known to rebel; against the Mujabbira, if He had willed it, He could not say He withheld provision so they would not rebel.
JISHUMI:v9p6253/r10.anchor: إذ لو أراد ذلك - كقول المجبرة - لما جاز أن يقول: لم أبسط الرزق لكيلا يفعل البغي

JISHUMI:v9p6255/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6255/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6255/r1.claim: God does not commit rebellion; since He is exalted above acts that occasion rebellion in others, He is even more exalted above rebellion itself.
JISHUMI:v9p6255/r1.anchor: وتدل على أنه لا يفعل البغي؛ لأنه تنزه على فعل ما يقع عنده البغي، فلأن ينزهه عن فعل البغي أولى

JISHUMI:v9p6255/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6255/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6255/r2.claim: Abundant provision can be a source of harm.
JISHUMI:v9p6255/r2.anchor: وتدل على أن بسط الرزق يكون مفسدة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p227#4/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p227#4/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p227#4/r1.claim: بغوا means injustice: the wealthy wrong one another; wealth breeds insolence, as Qarun shows.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p227#4/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p227#4/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p227#4/r2.claim: The Prophet said worldly flourishing and abundance were what he most feared for his community.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p227#4/r2.anchor: قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( 994 ) ( أخوف ما أخاف على أمتي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p227#4/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p227#4/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p227#4/r3.claim: An Arab verse depicts people revived by rain who then conceived plans for transgression and rivalry.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p227#4/r3.anchor: يعني : أنهم أحيوا فحدثوا أنفسهم بالبغي والتفانن

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p227#4/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p227#4/r4.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p227#4/r4.claim: Alternatively بغى means extravagance and pride, leading to arrogance, overreach, and corruption.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p227#4/r4.anchor: أو من البغي وهو البذخ والكبر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p227#4/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p227#4/r5.speaker: خباب ابن الأرت
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p227#4/r5.claim: Khabbab said it came down about people of the Suffa who coveted the wealth of Qurayza, Nadir, and Qaynuqa.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p227#4/r5.anchor: قال خباب ابن الأرت : فينا نزلت ، وذلك أنا نظرنا إلى أموال بني قريظة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p227#4/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p227#4/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p227#4/r6.claim: بقدر means by measured apportionment; the verb takes either of two verbal nouns.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p227#4/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p227#4/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p227#4/r7.claim: God knows how people's circumstances will turn out and apportions what best preserves their welfare by divine wisdom.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p227#4/r7.anchor: يعرف ما يؤول إليه أحوالهم ، فيقدر لهم ما هو أصلح لهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p227#4/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p227#4/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p227#4/r8.claim: Poverty makes transgression less common and abundance more common; universal prosperity would make it predominate, answering why some poor people transgress and some rich people do not.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p227#4/r8.anchor: لا شبهة في أن البغي مع الفقر أقل ومع البسط أكثر

NASAFI-FULL:v4p103/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p103/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p103/r1.claim: One sense of baghy is injustice: the rich would oppress one another, since wealth incites insolence; Qarun and Pharaoh are examples.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p103/r1.anchor: من البغى وهو الظلم اى لبغى هذا على ذاك وذاك على هذا لان الغنى مبطرة مأشرة وكفى بحال قارون وفرعون عبرة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p103/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p103/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p103/r2.claim: Alternatively, baghy means arrogance: people would become proud on earth.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p103/r2.anchor: أو من البغى وهو الكبر اى لتكبروا في الأرض

NASAFI-FULL:v4p103/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p103/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p103/r3.claim: Meccans and Abū ʿAmr read yunazzilu with a lightened zāy.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p103/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p103/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p103/r4.claim: The provision is apportioned by measure; the Arabic allows both qadr and qadar for the verbal noun of measuring.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p103/r4.anchor: ﴿ بقدر ما يشاء ﴾ بتقدير يقال قدره

NASAFI-FULL:v4p103/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p103/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p103/r5.claim: Allah knows people's states and assigns what wisdom requires—poverty or wealth, withholding or giving, constriction or expansion; universal wealth would cause oppression, while universal poverty would destroy them.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p103/r5.anchor: يعلم احوالهم فيقدر لهم ما تقتضيه حكمته فيفقر ويغنى ويمنع ويعطى ويقبض ويبسط ولو اغناهم جميعا لبغوا ولو افقرهم لهلكوا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p103/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p103/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p103/r6.claim: Oppression is rare both among the rich and the poor, but is less common in poverty and more common when provision is abundant.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p103/r6.anchor: وما ترى من البسط على من يبغى ومن البغى بدون البسط فهو قليل ولا شك ان البغى مع الفقر اقل ومع البسط اكثر واغلب

QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r1.speaker: قوم من أهل الصفة
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r1.claim: One report says the verse came when people of the Suffa wished for abundant provision.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r1.anchor: في نزولها قيل: إنها نزلت في قوم من أهل الصفة

QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r2.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r2.claim: Khabbab says it was revealed about them when they saw the wealth of Banu Nadir, Qurayza, and Qaynuqa and wished to have it.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r2.anchor: وقال خباب بن الأرت: فينا نزلت نظرنا إلى أموال بني النضير

QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r3.claim: Basata means to widen or spread; it may also be written with ṣād.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r3.anchor: ولو بسط } معناه وسع. وبسط الشيء نشره.

QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r4.claim: Baghaw means they would overstep and disobey.

QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas describes overreaching as seeking ever higher status, more mounts, vehicles, and clothing.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: بغيهم طلبهم منزلة بعد منزلة ودابة بعد دابة

QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r6.claim: One view says people given much would keep seeking more, supported by the report that Adam's son would want a third valley of gold after two.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r6.anchor: وقيل: أراد لو أعطاهم الكثير لطلبوا ما هو أكثر منه

QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r7.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r7.claim: Another view says equalizing everyone's wealth would end mutual dependence and cause crafts to cease.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r7.anchor: وقيل: لو جعلناهم سواء في المال لما انقاد بعضهم لبعض

QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r8.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r8.claim: Another view takes provision as rain: unceasing rain would distract people from prayer, so it is withheld to prompt supplication and granted so they can give thanks.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r8.anchor: وقيل: أراد بالرزق المطر الذي هو سبب الرزق

QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r9.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r9.claim: Another view says that when crops were abundant people raided one another, so baghy here can mean raiding.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r9.anchor: وقيل: كانوا إذا أخصبوا أغار بعضهم على بعض

QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r10.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes baghy as oppression: wealth makes people insolent and arrogant, as Qarun illustrates.

QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r11.claim: A prophetic report says the thing most feared for the community is the bloom and abundance of worldly life.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r11.anchor: كفى بقارون عبرة. ومنه قوله عليه السلام:

QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r12.speaker: شاعر من العرب
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r12.claim: An Arab poet's line about early rain growing trees between two tribes illustrates how prosperity could awaken thoughts of rivalry and mutual overreaching.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r12.anchor: ولبعض العرب: وقد جعل الوسمي ينبت بيننا وبين بني دودان

QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r13.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r13.claim: Baghy may instead mean extravagance and pride, leading to dominance and corruption on earth.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r13.anchor: أو من البغي وهو البذخ والكبر أي لتكبروا في الأرض

QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r14.claim: God measures people's provisions according to what suffices them.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r14.anchor: أي ينزل أرزاقهم بقدر ما يشاء لكفايتهم

QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r15.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r15.claim: Muqatil says God makes whomever He wills rich and whomever He wills poor.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r15.anchor: وقال مقاتل: «ينزل بقدر ما يشاء» يجعل من يشاء غنيا

QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r16.speaker: علماؤنا
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r16.claim: God's acts always have wisdom, though He is not obliged to choose what is most beneficial; He may withhold wealth from someone whose prosperity would lead to corruption.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r16.anchor: قال علماؤنا: أفعال الرب سبحانه لا تخلو عن مصالح

QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r17.speaker: علماؤنا
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r17.claim: Poverty is not disgrace and wealth is not virtue; God's acts remain subject to His will rather than a rule of benefit in every case.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27/r17.anchor: فليس ضيق الرزق هوانا ولا سعة الرزق فضيلة

QURTUBI-FULL:42:27#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27#2/r1.claim: Anas transmits a divine report: harming God's friend is war; God hastens to aid friends, and a servant approaches through obligations then extra worship until beloved, when God answers requests and supports him.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27#2/r1.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فيما يرويه عن ربه تبارك وتعالى قال: «من أهان لي وليا

QURTUBI-FULL:42:27#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27#2/r2.speaker: الله تعالى
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27#2/r2.claim: In the report, God says He knows which believers are harmed by a particular worship practice, poverty, or wealth, and manages each according to their hearts.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27#2/r2.anchor: وإن من عبادي المؤمنين من يسألني الباب من العبادة

QURTUBI-FULL:42:27#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27#2/r3.speaker: أنس
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27#2/r3.claim: Anas ends by asking God not to impoverish him, since he is among the believers only improved by wealth.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:27#2/r3.anchor: ثم قال أنس: اللهم إني من عبادك المؤمنين الذين لا يصلحهم إلا الغنى
